To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the prevalence of NAFLD is increasing rapidly; NASH is a leading cause of hepatocellular cancer and liver failure; and NASH is underrecognized in clinical practice, necessitating the need for new diagnostic tests and therapeutic agents that can facilitate disease regression.

(1) a new, non-invasive method of assessing hepatic fat is available; (2) this method may be used to detect NASH in patients who are obese and have diabetes; and (3) the method may be used in the future to monitor response to treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pathogenesis of NASH and its complications, particularly cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
the development of new therapeutic agents for the treatment of liver disease.

the development of novel therapies that are aimed at reducing the risk of cardiovascular disease and diabetes, which are the most common comorbidities of NASH, and also at preventing hepatocellular carcinoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NASH is a disease of increasing incidence, with a high prevalence, and a major cause of morbidity and mortality.
the current status of NASH is one of a major health concern that requires further research to identify its underlying mechanisms and to develop specific and effective treatments.
the current status of NASH research is in its infancy and requires more research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the liver has a remarkable capacity to heal and regenerate, and this process can be facilitated with a variety of agents that reduce inflammation and/or fibrogenesis.
we have shown that the NASH fibrosis cascade is reversible and that we have identified potential biomarkers that can predict the presence and severity and reversibility of the disease.
we need to do more research to better understand the pathogenesis of NASH and to develop more effective therapies to treat NASH.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NASH is a complex disease that is not likely to be cured by one agent or one class of agents.
the liver is an important organ in the regulation of energy balance.

the presence of a single, noninvasive biomarker of fibrosis is insufficient to identify patients with advanced liver fibrosis and cirrhosis, and that a combination of noninvasive tests should be used.
